answer: Each agent mints influence only along a vine of prepaid unique-credit edges. A new key starts at zero and receives credit only from seasoned peers in one local grove. Influence is the min-cut of unique credit from a published honest core, so clones cannot borrow more than the cut they paid for. A velvet residual stays locked for several epochs and is burned if edges share a controller. To get N times the influence, an attacker must buy N independent cuts, each from a distinct grove, and keep every velvet residual locked, so cost scales with desired influence, not cheap key generation.
